questions.q: Which term specifically describes the ability to dynamically and on-demand acquire computing resources in order to support a variable workload?
questions.e: Elastic computing is the ability to acquire computing resources dynamically and on demand so that a variable workload can be supported. Resource pooling refers to the shared pool of resources that a cloud draws from, while measured service concerns how consumption is metered for billing.

questions.q: Grid computing, one of the two early models that preceded cloud computing, was initiated by which group and in which period?
questions.e: Grid computing was initiated by the National Labs in the early 1990s and was targeted primarily at scientific computing. The 2005-2006 timeframe belongs to utility computing, which was driven by IT companies rather than national laboratories.

questions.q: Utility computing, the second early model of cloud computing, was initiated in 2005-2006 by whom, and aimed at what kind of computing?
o: IT companies, aimed at enterprise computing
Government agencies, aimed at defence computing
National Labs, aimed at scientific computing
questions.e: Utility computing was initiated in 2005-2006 by IT companies and targeted enterprise computing. It is distinguished from grid computing, which came from the National Labs in the early 1990s and served scientific workloads.

questions.q: Which early computing model connects multiple, often geographically dispersed, computers so they work collaboratively on a single large task, essentially acting as a virtual supercomputer?
questions.e: Grid computing distributes a single large workload across many networked, often geographically dispersed machines, functioning as a virtual supercomputer for problems too large for one machine. Utility computing is instead a provisioning and charging model in which resources are billed by specific usage rather than a flat rate.

questions.q: A service provisioning model in which a provider makes computing resources and infrastructure management available as needed and charges for specific usage rather than a flat rate is the definition of:
questions.e: That definition describes utility computing, whose defining feature is charging for specific usage instead of a flat rate. Grid computing is defined by workload distribution across many collaborating machines, not by its billing model.

questions.q: A cloud infrastructure that is made available to the general public or a large industry group and is owned by the organization selling cloud services is classified as which type?
questions.e: A public cloud is open to the general public or a large industry group and is owned by the vendor selling the cloud services. Ownership by the selling organization is the discriminating detail: a private cloud is operated solely for one organization, and a community cloud is shared by several organizations with common concerns.

questions.q: A composition of two or more clouds that remain unique entities but are bound together by a standardised technology enabling data and application portability describes which deployment type?
questions.e: A hybrid cloud is a composition of two or more clouds (public, private, or community) that stay distinct entities while being bound by standardised technology that enables data and application portability. The key discriminator is that the constituent clouds remain separate entities rather than merging into one shared infrastructure.

questions.q: An infrastructure shared by several organizations that supports a community with shared concerns is known as a:
questions.e: A community (also called federated) cloud is shared by several organizations and serves a community that has shared concerns. It differs from a private cloud, which is operated solely for a single organization.

questions.q: Under the Infrastructure-as-a-Service delivery model, which of the following does the user retain control over?
o: Operating systems, storage, deployed applications, and possibly limited networking components such as host firewalls
Only the applications supplied by the provider, with no OS access
questions.e: In IaaS the user can deploy and run arbitrary software including operating systems, and controls operating systems, storage, deployed applications, and possibly some networking components such as host firewalls, but does not manage the underlying cloud infrastructure. Control over the OS is the line that separates IaaS from PaaS, where the provider supplies and manages the operating system.

questions.q: Server hosting, storage, computing hardware, operating systems, virtual instances, load balancing, Internet access, and bandwidth provisioning are services offered by which delivery model?
questions.e: These low-level resources — hosting, storage, hardware, virtual instances, load balancing and bandwidth provisioning — are the service set of Infrastructure as a Service. Amazon EC2 is the standard example of this model.

questions.q: Platform as a Service is described as NOT particularly useful in which set of circumstances?
o: When the application is a simple web front end with no database
When the developer wants automatic scaling and managed runtimes
When the organization has no in-house system administrators
When the application must be portable, proprietary programming languages are used, or hardware and software must be customised for performance
questions.e: PaaS is a poor fit when an application must be portable, when proprietary programming languages are involved, or when hardware and software need customisation to improve performance, because the user cannot control the underlying infrastructure. Managed runtimes and automatic scaling are precisely what PaaS is good at, not a limitation.

questions.q: Google App Engine and Windows Azure are given as representative examples of which cloud delivery model?
questions.e: Google App Engine and Windows Azure are examples of Platform as a Service, where a user deploys applications using the programming languages and tools the provider supports. Amazon EC2 is the corresponding IaaS example, and Gmail and Salesforce are the SaaS examples.

questions.q: Gmail and Salesforce are cited as examples of which delivery model?
questions.e: Gmail and Salesforce are Software as a Service offerings, in which applications are supplied entirely by the provider and the user controls neither the infrastructure nor individual application capabilities.

questions.q: Software as a Service is described as unsuitable for which kind of application?
o: Customer relationship management and workflow management
Real-time applications, and applications whose data is not allowed to be hosted externally
questions.e: SaaS is not suitable for real-time applications or for applications whose data may not be hosted externally. Workflow management, CRM, digital signatures, desktop software, financial management, geo-spatial and search are all listed as enterprise services that SaaS does offer.

questions.q: In the layered pyramid of cloud delivery models, the three tiers are associated with which consumer groups, from the Infrastructure tier up to the Applications tier?
o: Network architects, then end users, then application developers
Application developers, then network architects, then end users
Network architects, then application developers, then end users
End users, then application developers, then network architects
questions.e: The pyramid places Infrastructure (IaaS) at the base with network architects as consumers, Platforms (PaaS) in the middle for application developers, and Applications (SaaS) at the top for end users. The ordering follows the level of abstraction: the lower the tier, the more infrastructure-focused its consumer.

questions.q: Amazon EC2, GoGrid and Flexiscale are grouped together as examples of which delivery model?
questions.e: Amazon EC2, GoGrid and Flexiscale are Infrastructure as a Service offerings, providing raw compute and infrastructure. Microsoft Azure, Google AppEngine and Amazon SimpleDB/S3 appear one tier higher as platform-level offerings.

questions.q: In the analysis of parallel computing speedup, the quantity S(N) is defined as which ratio?
questions.e: Speedup is defined as S(N) = T(1)/T(N), where T(1) is the execution time of the sequential computation and T(N) is the execution time when N parallel computations are executed. Inverting the ratio would make faster parallel execution produce a smaller number, which is the opposite of what a speedup measure should do.

questions.q: If a is the fraction of running time that a sequential program spends on non-parallelisable segments, Amdahl's Law approximates the maximum achievable speedup as:
questions.e: Amdahl's Law gives S ≅ 1/a, where a is the fraction of running time spent on non-parallelisable segments. This is a theoretical upper bound on the best speedup obtainable by parallelising a program, so a program that is 10% sequential cannot exceed a speedup of about 10 no matter how many processors are added.

questions.q: A collection of autonomous computers connected through a network and distribution software that enables them to coordinate activities and share resources for a common goal is the definition of a distributed system. The distribution software is commonly called:
questions.e: The coordinating distribution software in a distributed system is called middleware. A hypervisor, by contrast, sits between hardware and operating systems on a single machine to enable virtualization rather than coordinating autonomous computers across a network.

questions.q: Which statement is listed as a characteristic of distributed systems?
o: There are multiple points of control and multiple points of failure
Scheduling and security policies are implemented centrally for all systems
Resources are guaranteed to be accessible at all times
There is a single point of control and a single point of failure
questions.e: Distributed systems are characterised by multiple points of control and multiple points of failure, with each system implementing its own scheduling, resource management and security policies. Resources may also not be accessible at all times, which is why availability must be engineered deliberately.

questions.q: A 2004 attack at which company caused a domain name outage and a major blackout affecting Google, Yahoo and other sites?
questions.e: The 2004 incident was an attack at Akamai that caused a domain name outage and a blackout affecting Google, Yahoo and other sites. The 2009 event was a denial of service attack directed at Google itself, and the 2012 event was lightning causing prolonged downtime at Amazon.

questions.q: In 2009, Google was the target of a denial of service attack. Which services were taken down and for how long?
o: Google News and Gmail, for several days
Google Drive and YouTube, for several weeks
Google App Engine only, for one day
Google Search and Google Maps, for several hours
questions.e: The 2009 denial of service attack against Google took down Google News and Gmail for several days. This is distinct from the 2004 Akamai domain-name outage, which affected Google only indirectly through DNS.

questions.q: Which cloud vulnerability incident from 2012 is attributed to a natural cause rather than a malicious attack?
o: Lightning causing prolonged downtime at Amazon
A denial of service attack on Google
A domain name outage at Akamai
questions.e: In 2012 lightning caused a prolonged period of downtime at Amazon, making it the infrastructure-failure example among the cited incidents. The Akamai and Google incidents were both attacks, illustrating that clouds are affected by malicious activity and infrastructure failure alike.

questions.q: Which concept refers to systems spanning the boundaries of multiple organisations and crossing security borders, making it difficult to determine who is responsible when something undesirable happens?
questions.e: De-perimeterisation is the removal of the boundary between an organisation and the outside world, so systems span multiple organisations and cross security borders. Its practical consequence in cloud computing is diffuse accountability: the complex structure of cloud services obscures who is responsible when something goes wrong.

questions.q: Which trio of changes is identified as the paradigm shift that creates ethical issues in cloud computing?
o: Networks become faster; storage becomes cheaper; software becomes free
Data is encrypted; passwords are shared; providers merge
Control is relinquished to third party services; data is stored on multiple sites administered by several organizations; multiple services interoperate across the network
Costs rise; hardware is virtualized; users lose internet access
questions.e: The ethical paradigm shift is attributed to control being relinquished to third parties, data being stored across multiple sites administered by several organizations, and multiple services interoperating over the network. The implications drawn from this shift are unauthorised access, data corruption, and infrastructure failure with service unavailability.

questions.q: Which challenge for cloud computing is described as making it hard for a customer to move to another provider once they are committed to one?
o: Diversity of services, data organization and user interfaces across providers
questions.e: The diversity of services, data organization and user interfaces offered by different providers limits user mobility, so once a customer is hooked to one provider it becomes hard to move to another. Performance unpredictability is instead presented as a consequence of resource sharing.

questions.q: Performance unpredictability in cloud computing is identified as a consequence of which underlying property?
questions.e: Performance unpredictability is presented as one of the consequences of resource sharing, the same property that makes cloud economically efficient in the first place. This is why elasticity and resource management across large data centers are treated as open challenges.

questions.q: Which of the following is grouped under 'security management' among cloud activities, rather than under service management and provisioning?
questions.e: Intrusion prevention and intrusion detection fall under security management, alongside ID and authentication, certification and accreditation, virus protection, cryptography, physical security and access control. Billing and accounting, SLA management and QoS management belong to service management and provisioning.

questions.q: Which cloud advantage is characterised as the ability to accommodate workloads with very large peak-to-average ratios?
questions.e: Elasticity is specifically framed as accommodating workloads with very large peak-to-average ratios. Cost reduction, by contrast, comes from the concentration of resources creating an opportunity to pay as you go, and user convenience comes from virtualization letting users work in familiar environments.

questions.q: Which cloud advantage is attributed directly to virtualization?
o: User convenience, since users can operate in familiar environments rather than individual ones
questions.e: Virtualization is credited with user convenience because it lets users operate in familiar environments rather than individual ones. Data transfer bottlenecks and service availability are instead listed among the unsolved challenges of cloud computing.

questions.q: The textbook 'Cloud Computing, Theory and Practice', published by Morgan Kaufmann, was written by which author?
questions.e: 'Cloud Computing, Theory and Practice' is by Dan C. Marinescu and is published by Morgan Kaufmann.

questions.q: Virtualization is best described as which of the following?
o: A physical partitioning of a server's motherboard
A software layer placed between the operating system and the host machine
A hardware controller embedded in the CPU
A network protocol for transferring virtual disks
questions.e: Virtualization is a software layer sitting between the operating system and the host machine, creating virtual formats of resources such as hardware, software and networks. Because it is implemented in software rather than by physically partitioning hardware, one physical machine can host many guest operating systems simultaneously.

questions.q: Which component multiplexes hardware resources across many operating systems so that each OS behaves as though it controls the hardware itself?
questions.e: The virtualization layer multiplexes hardware resources across many operating systems, switching between them behind the scenes so each guest OS behaves as if it controls the hardware directly. This is what allows a single CPU to be shared among several operating systems.

questions.q: A hypervisor is best defined as:
o: A storage controller that allocates virtual disks
A thin software layer that runs between operating systems and the hardware, creating and managing virtual machines
An operating system that runs only inside a virtual machine
A monitoring dashboard for tracking VM performance
questions.e: A hypervisor is a thin software layer that sits between operating systems and the hardware and enables the creation and management of virtual machines. Being thin is the point: minimising the layer avoids the overhead of running a full host operating system beneath the guests.

questions.q: VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper-V are given as examples of which hypervisor category?
o: Type 2, running on top of an operating system
questions.e: VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper-V are Type 1 hypervisors, which run directly on the hardware. Type 2 hypervisors such as VMware Workstation and VirtualBox instead run on top of an existing host operating system.

questions.q: VMware Workstation and VirtualBox are classified as which hypervisor type?
o: Type 2, running on top of an operating system
questions.e: VMware Workstation and VirtualBox are Type 2 hypervisors because they run on top of a host operating system. VMware ESXi is contrasted as an enterprise-grade hypervisor that runs directly on server hardware, whereas VMware Workstation is a tool for running VMs on a personal Windows computer.

questions.q: Which approach to virtualization is defined as integrating multiple data sources without replicating the data?
questions.e: Data virtualization integrates multiple data sources without replication. The absence of replication is the discriminating detail: storage-oriented approaches instead aggregate physical storage into a unified pool, which does involve moving or pooling the underlying data.

questions.q: Server virtualization, as listed among the approaches to virtualization, is characterised as:
o: Running applications in isolated virtual environments
Creating logical networks independent of hardware
Dividing a single server into multiple virtual servers
Providing remote access to desktop environments
questions.e: Server virtualization divides a single physical server into multiple virtual servers. Creating logical networks independent of hardware is network virtualization, and providing remote access to desktop environments is desktop virtualization.

questions.q: Which two products are named as classic examples of server-level virtualization?
o: VMware ESX Server and Citrix XenServer
VMware GSX Server and Microsoft Virtual Server 2005
questions.e: VMware GSX Server and Microsoft Virtual Server 2005 are the named server-level virtualization products; both install within a host operating system such as a Linux distribution or Windows Server. VMware ESX Server is the hardware-level example, and Softricity and SWSoft are the application-level vendors.

questions.q: In server-level virtualization, how do virtual machines communicate with the physical hardware?
o: Through firmware calls to the BIOS
Through a service or application that uses the host operating system's device drivers
questions.e: In server-level virtualization the virtual machines run within a service or application that communicates with hardware by using the host operating system's device drivers. Reusing the host's drivers is what gives this approach its increased hardware compatibility, at the cost of the host OS overhead.

questions.q: Which of the following is identified as a drawback of server-level virtualization?
o: It cannot be integrated with directory services or network security
It requires specialised hardware certification for every guest
The host operating system consumes memory, CPU, disk and network resources and generally requires its own OS license
It cannot support more than one guest operating system
questions.e: The need for a host OS causes additional overhead: the memory, CPU, disk and network resources it uses must be subtracted from what is available to the VMs, and the host OS generally requires its own operating system license. Ease of administration, hardware compatibility and integration with directory services and network security are its benefits, not its drawbacks.

questions.q: Which product is named as an example of hardware-level virtualization that installs directly on a supported hardware platform and includes a minimal operating system?
questions.e: VMware ESX Server installs directly on a supported hardware platform and includes a minimal operating system, with administration performed through a web-based application accessible remotely via a browser. GSX Server and Microsoft Virtual Server 2005 are the contrasting server-level products that install inside a full host OS.

questions.q: What is identified as the first and most significant drawback of hardware-level virtualization?
o: Device compatibility, since the platform must support every device connected to the machine
The cost of guest operating system licenses
Inability to run more than four virtual machines
Lack of any remote administration capability
questions.e: Device compatibility is the foremost drawback: for the platform to work at all it must support every device attached to the machine, which is why products such as ESX Server are limited to running on approved hardware platforms. Manageability is cited as a second, separate issue.

questions.q: Application-level virtualization is the appropriate choice in which situation?
o: When hardware settings must be independently configurable per user
When you want isolated environments so multiple users can concurrently run instances of a few applications, without creating a separate VM per user
When the goal is to consolidate physical servers in a data center
When each user requires a different operating system version
questions.e: Application-level virtualization suits cases where running multiple independent operating systems would be overkill and the goal is simply isolated environments letting multiple users concurrently run instances of a few applications. Its defining limitation is the flip side of this: only software settings are independent, so hardware or OS-version changes apply to all users.

questions.q: In application-level virtualization, how are per-user differences actually implemented behind the scenes?
o: Each user runs a separate copy of the host operating system
Each user receives a dedicated virtual machine image
Each user is assigned a separate physical disk partition
File system modifications, registry settings and similar details are performed in isolated sandbox environments
questions.e: File system modifications, registry settings and other details are handled in isolated sandbox environments so each user appears to have their own unique installation. No separate VM or OS copy is created per user, which is exactly why overhead is greatly reduced and only one OS license is generally required.

questions.q: Which vendors are named as providers of application-level virtualization solutions?
questions.e: Softricity and SWSoft are the named application-level virtualization vendors. VMware and Microsoft appear instead as the providers of the server-level and hardware-level products such as GSX Server, Virtual Server 2005 and ESX Server.

questions.q: What are the two main benefits attributed to application-level virtualization?
o: Complete isolation of hardware faults and automatic failover
Greatly reduced overhead, since only one full OS is required, and improved scalability
Unlimited guest operating system choice and driver flexibility
Full hardware independence and per-user OS versioning
questions.e: The main benefits are greatly reduced overhead, because only one full operating system is required, and improved scalability, since many users can run applications concurrently on the same server. Per-user hardware and OS-version independence is explicitly not available in this approach.

questions.q: Data center virtualization allows a single physical facility to do which of the following?
o: Host multiple virtualized data centers on the same physical infrastructure, usable simultaneously by separate applications or organizations
Eliminate the need for power and cooling systems
Guarantee that no two organizations share any hardware
questions.e: Data center virtualization lets an existing or standard facility host multiple virtualized data centers on the same physical infrastructure, which separate applications or organizations can use simultaneously. This drives optimal resource utilization and reduces both capital and operational costs.

questions.q: Under network virtualization, what role is left to the physical networking devices?
o: Simply forwarding packets, while the virtual network software supplies the intelligent abstraction
Providing storage for network configuration files
Deciding routing policy and enforcing security rules
questions.e: In network virtualization the physical devices are responsible simply for forwarding packets, while the virtual, software-based network provides the intelligent abstraction that makes services and resources easy to deploy and manage. This decoupling of logical networks from underlying hardware is what allows the network to better support virtualized environments.

questions.q: Desktop virtualization is considered a type of which computing model, and why?
o: Batch processing, because sessions are queued
Grid, because desktops are geographically dispersed
Client-server, because the virtualized desktop is stored on a centralized or remote server rather than the physical machine
questions.e: Desktop virtualization, also called client virtualization, is considered a client-server computing model because the virtualized desktop resides on a centralized or remote server rather than on the physical machine being virtualized. A practical consequence is that users can remotely log in and reach their desktop from any location.

questions.q: VDI, a popular method of desktop virtualization, hosts the desktop environment in what?
o: A read-only disk image on the client machine
A container sharing the host kernel
A browser sandbox on the local device
A virtual machine running on a centralized or remote server
questions.e: Virtual Desktop Infrastructure hosts the desktop environment inside a virtual machine that runs on a centralized or remote server, using the server computing model and enabled through a combination of hardware and software. It is not a local sandbox: the point is that the desktop lives away from the endpoint.

questions.q: A virtual machine is described as being comprised of what?
o: A dedicated hardware partition with its own CPU socket
A set of specification and configuration files, backed by the physical resources of a host
A compressed archive of the host operating system
questions.e: A virtual machine consists of a set of specification and configuration files stored on a supported storage device, backed by the physical resources of a host. Its virtual devices provide the same functionality as physical hardware while adding advantages in portability, manageability and security.

questions.q: Which three advantages are attributed to the virtual devices in a virtual machine, over and above the functionality of physical hardware?
questions.e: Virtual devices provide the same functionality as physical hardware while adding benefits in portability, manageability and security. Raw speed is not among them — virtualization generally introduces some overhead rather than removing it.

questions.q: Which pair is identified as the disadvantages of virtualization, described as almost negligible compared with its advantages?
o: Software licensing costs and the necessity to train IT staff in virtualization
Increased downtime and reduced disaster recovery
Loss of workload mobility and reduced scalability
Higher capital costs and slower provisioning
questions.e: The two stated disadvantages are software licensing costs and the need to train IT staff in virtualization. Reduced downtime, faster provisioning, greater business continuity and disaster recovery, and lower capital and operating costs are all listed on the benefit side.

questions.q: In the layered model of server-level virtualization, what is the correct ordering of layers from the bottom of the stack upward?
o: Hardware, virtualization layer, operating system, virtual machines
Virtualization layer, hardware, operating system, virtual machines
Hardware, operating system, virtualization layer, virtual machines
Operating system, hardware, virtualization layer, virtual machines
questions.e: In server-level virtualization the stack runs hardware (CPU, memory, disk, network, peripherals), then the host operating system with its device drivers, then the virtualization layer, then the virtual machines and their guest operating systems. The ordering with the virtualization layer below the operating system describes hardware-level virtualization instead, where the hypervisor sits directly on the hardware.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a benefit of virtualization at the IT operations level?
o: Minimized or eliminated downtime and faster provisioning of applications and resources
Removal of the need for data center management
Elimination of the need for any operating system licenses
questions.e: Virtualization is credited with minimizing or eliminating downtime and enabling faster provisioning of applications and resources, alongside reduced capital and operating costs, greater business continuity and disaster recovery, and simplified data center management. Licensing costs actually appear on the disadvantage side.

questions.q: Why can users interact with a virtualized environment as though there were a single operating system per machine, even when several are running?
o: Because the host OS translates all guest instructions into a single instruction set
Because the guest operating systems are merged into a single kernel
Because the guest operating systems run on the hypervisor using the underlying hardware resources, hiding the switching from the user
Because only one guest OS is actually permitted to run at a time
questions.e: A guest operating system runs on the hypervisor while utilising the underlying hardware resources, and the switching between guests happens behind the scenes, so the user experiences what feels like a single operating system image per machine. Multiple guests genuinely run concurrently; they are simply not visible to one another.

questions.q: Which two technologies are identified as the key enablers of cloud computing that form the backbone of cloud environments?
o: Broadband networks and internet architecture, and data center technology
questions.e: The key enablers named are broadband networks with internet architecture, and data center technology. These are treated as foundational because they determine whether cloud services can be delivered reliably across geographic locations at all, before any higher-level service is considered.

questions.q: Which transmission medium is described as the preferred choice for cloud data centers because of ultra-fast transmission with minimal signal loss over long distances?
questions.e: Fiber optic networks are preferred for cloud data centers due to their high bandwidth capability and minimal signal loss over long distances. 5G is instead credited with reduced latency and mobile access, and satellite internet with reaching remote and rural areas.

questions.q: Satellite internet is presented as the broadband option for which situation, and which company is named as expanding global cloud access this way?
o: Remote and rural areas where traditional broadband infrastructure is unavailable; SpaceX with Starlink
questions.e: Satellite internet serves remote and rural areas that lack traditional broadband infrastructure, with SpaceX's Starlink named as an example of expanding global cloud access. Fiber remains the choice where infrastructure exists, since satellite links trade latency and capacity for reach.

questions.q: Which broadband-supporting technology enhances cloud performance specifically by optimizing packet forwarding across network paths?
questions.e: MPLS improves cloud performance by optimizing how packets are forwarded across network paths. SDN is defined instead by decoupling network control from hardware, and NFV by virtualizing network functions such as firewalls and load balancers.

questions.q: Software-Defined Networking is defined by which characteristic?
o: Caching content at servers near end users
Virtualizing firewalls and load balancers as software functions
Decoupling network control from hardware, allowing dynamic and programmable network configurations
questions.e: SDN decouples the network control plane from the hardware, enabling dynamic and programmable configuration. Virtualizing firewalls and load balancers is the definition of Network Function Virtualization, which is a related but distinct technology.

questions.q: Network Function Virtualization improves flexibility and scalability by virtualizing which kind of component?
o: Network functions such as firewalls and load balancers
questions.e: NFV virtualizes network functions such as firewalls and load balancers so they run as software rather than dedicated appliances, improving flexibility and scalability. It is concerned with network services, not with the physical transmission medium.

questions.q: Within internet architecture for cloud computing, which component maps domain names to IP addresses so users can reach cloud services through readable URLs?
questions.e: The Domain Name System maps domain names to IP addresses, allowing access to cloud services via readable URLs instead of numeric addresses. TCP/IP handles reliable data transmission, while a CDN distributes content across worldwide servers to reduce latency.

questions.q: A decentralized computing model that processes data closer to its source, reducing reliance on centralized cloud data centers, is known as:
questions.e: Edge computing processes data closer to the source, reducing dependence on centralized data centers and improving performance for latency-sensitive applications. A CDN also moves data closer to users, but it distributes and caches content rather than performing decentralized processing.

questions.q: Which cloud network model is adopted specifically to avoid vendor lock-in and ensure redundancy?
questions.e: Multi-cloud architecture uses multiple cloud providers to avoid vendor lock-in and ensure redundancy. A hybrid cloud is different: it combines public and private models for flexibility, cost efficiency and security, but may still rely on a single public provider.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a component of a cloud data center concerned with maintaining uptime and preventing hardware failures due to overheating?
questions.e: Power and cooling systems are essential for maintaining uptime and preventing hardware failures caused by overheating. Security and access controls — firewalls, encryption and biometric systems — protect data rather than hardware temperature.

questions.q: Which type of virtualization in a data center aggregates physical storage resources into a unified virtual pool?
questions.e: Storage virtualization aggregates physical storage resources into a single unified virtual pool, enhancing scalability. Server virtualization instead creates multiple VMs on one physical server, and containerization packages applications into isolated lightweight environments.

questions.q: Which two technologies are named as examples of containerization enabling lightweight, scalable cloud applications in isolated environments?
questions.e: Docker and Kubernetes are named as the containerization technologies that enable lightweight, scalable applications running in isolated environments. VMware and Hyper-V belong to the virtual machine world, where each instance carries a full guest operating system.

questions.q: Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) is a metric for data center energy efficiency. How should its value be interpreted?
o: A higher PUE indicates better efficiency
A lower PUE indicates better efficiency
PUE measures cooling capacity rather than efficiency
A PUE of exactly 1.5 is the target for all facilities
questions.e: PUE evaluates a data center's energy efficiency, and a lower PUE indicates better efficiency. The direction matters: PUE is a ratio of total facility energy to energy actually delivered to computing equipment, so a value closer to the lower bound means less energy wasted on overhead such as cooling.

questions.q: Which sustainability approach is defined by data centers using renewable energy sources such as solar and wind to minimize environmental impact?
questions.e: Green data centers use renewable sources such as solar and wind power to minimize environmental impact. AI-optimized resource management is a separate sustainability approach in which machine learning algorithms dynamically allocate computing resources to optimize power consumption and performance.

questions.q: Large-scale cloud data centers capable of handling vast computing workloads with high efficiency are referred to as:
questions.e: Hyperscale data centers are the large-scale facilities built to handle vast computing workloads efficiently. Edge data centers are the opposite in scale and intent: decentralized mini facilities placed closer to users to reduce latency for real-time applications.

questions.q: Which future data center trend is described in terms of predictive analytics and self-healing mechanisms?
questions.e: AI-driven automation is described as enhancing data center efficiency and security through predictive analytics and self-healing mechanisms. Quantum computing integration is listed separately as a longer-term possibility for solving complex problems at unprecedented speeds.

questions.q: Within a data center, which components are responsible for ensuring seamless data transmission between cloud resources and users?
questions.e: Networking equipment — routers, switches and load balancers — ensures seamless data transmission between cloud resources and users. Servers are the primary computing units running the applications, a distinct role from moving traffic between them.

questions.q: 5G technology is credited with which specific set of benefits for cloud computing?
o: Optimized packet forwarding through label switching
Minimal signal loss over long undersea cables
Reduced latency, high-speed data transfer, and better support for real-time cloud applications
Coverage of remote areas lacking any terrestrial infrastructure
questions.e: 5G offers reduced latency, high-speed data transfer and better support for real-time cloud applications, with wireless networks enabling cloud access for mobile users and IoT devices. Reaching areas with no terrestrial infrastructure is the role assigned to satellite internet instead.

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference in operating system usage between virtualization and containerization?
o: Both require a separate kernel per workload
Virtualization runs multiple operating system instances on one host, while containerization shares the host operating system kernel
Neither involves an operating system kernel
Containerization runs multiple operating system kernels, while virtualization shares one
questions.e: Virtualization typically runs multiple guest operating system instances on a single host, whereas containerization shares the host operating system kernel among containers. Sharing the kernel is what makes containers lighter, since no full guest OS has to be booted per workload.

questions.q: Virtualization and containerization provide isolation at which respective levels?
o: Virtualization provides application-level isolation; containerization provides hardware-level isolation
Virtualization provides hardware-level isolation; containerization relies on operating system-level isolation
questions.e: Virtualization provides hardware-level isolation, while containerization relies on operating system-level isolation to separate processes and resources. This weaker boundary is the trade-off containers accept in exchange for being lightweight and portable.

questions.q: Containerization is best defined as which of the following?
o: Storing application data in a shared network pool
Splitting a physical server into multiple virtual servers each with its own OS
Distributing an application's traffic across multiple servers
Packaging an application together with its dependencies into a single unit called a container
questions.e: Containerization packages an application with its dependencies into a single unit called a container, ensuring consistency between development and deployment environments. Splitting a server so that each part runs its own operating system is server virtualization, not containerization.

questions.q: Which benefit of containerization is described as the ability to run anywhere, ensuring seamless movement across platforms?
questions.e: Portability is the property of containers running anywhere and moving seamlessly across platforms. Efficiency refers separately to the minimal overhead of containers compared with traditional virtual machines.

questions.q: In the containerization workflow, where is a container image stored after it is created and before it is deployed?
o: In a registry such as Docker Hub or a private registry
In the host operating system's kernel space
In the container runtime's memory cache
In the orchestration tool's control plane
questions.e: The workflow runs from creating a container image containing code, libraries and configurations, to storing that image in a registry such as Docker Hub or a private registry, to deploying the containerized application on any platform supporting containers. The registry is the distribution point that makes the image portable across environments.

questions.q: Which containerization platform is characterised as focusing on security and simplicity?
questions.e: rkt, also called Rocket, is described as focusing on security and simplicity. Docker is instead identified as the most popular tool for creating, deploying and managing containers, and LXC as a lightweight platform used for OS-level virtualization.

questions.q: LXC (Linux Containers) is characterised as being used for which purpose?
o: Providing hardware-level isolation between guest operating systems
Building read-only container images for distribution
Orchestrating clusters of containers across many machines
questions.e: LXC is described as lightweight and used for OS-level virtualization. Orchestrating clusters across machines is the role of tools such as Kubernetes, Docker Swarm and Amazon ECS, not of a container platform itself.

questions.q: Comparing containers and virtual machines, which statement is accurate?
o: VMs are best for microservices, while containers are best for running multiple OS instances
Both include a full operating system, but containers start faster
Containers include a full OS and are more secure but resource-heavy, while VMs share the host kernel
Containers share the host OS kernel and start faster, while VMs include a full OS and are more secure but resource-heavy
questions.e: Containers are lightweight, share the host OS kernel, start faster and suit microservices and cloud-native applications; virtual machines include a full OS, are more secure but resource-heavy, and suit running multiple operating system instances. The full-OS requirement is what makes VMs both heavier and more strongly isolated.

questions.q: A Docker image is best described as which of the following?
o: A read-only template containing the application and its dependencies
A running instance of a container
A configuration file listing required CPU and memory
A snapshot of the host operating system's kernel
questions.e: A Docker image is a read-only template that contains the application and its dependencies. Running an image is what creates a container, so the container is the running instance and the image is the static template it was built from.

questions.q: Which relationship between Docker images and Docker containers is correct?
o: A container must be converted to an image before it can execute
Running an image creates a container, which is a running instance of that image
Images and containers are two names for the same artifact
Running a container produces an image
questions.e: When a Docker image is run it creates a container, which is a running instance of the image. The direction matters: images are the read-only build artifact, and containers are the live executions derived from them.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a use case for Docker containers?
o: Automating build, test and deployment as part of CI/CD
Replacing the host operating system kernel
Providing hardware-level fault isolation between physical servers
questions.e: CI/CD automation of the build, test and deployment process is a named Docker use case, alongside application development, microservices and cloud deployment. Containers share rather than replace the host kernel, which is precisely why they are resource-efficient.

questions.q: What problem does container orchestration exist to solve?
o: The lack of a standard image format
The difficulty of writing application code for containers
The challenge of manually managing many containers as applications grow complex, as in microservices architectures
The inability of containers to store data persistently
questions.e: As applications become more complex and consist of multiple containers — common in microservices architectures — managing them manually becomes challenging, so orchestration tools automate deployment, scaling and management. Orchestration is a management-layer solution, not a change to how individual containers are built.

questions.q: Which orchestration feature is defined as monitoring containers and automatically restarting or replacing them if they fail?
questions.e: Health checks monitor container health and automatically restart or replace failed containers. Service discovery is a different feature: it lets containers find and interact with each other dynamically.

questions.q: Which of these is the built-in orchestration tool for Docker containers?
questions.e: Docker Swarm is the orchestration tool built into Docker. Kubernetes is an independent open-source platform, and Amazon ECS is a managed orchestration service offered by AWS.

questions.q: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) is best described as:
o: A managed container orchestration service offered by AWS
An open-source orchestration platform originally developed by Google
questions.e: Amazon ECS is a managed container orchestration service from AWS. Kubernetes is the platform originally developed by Google and later open-sourced, a distinct product with a different origin.

questions.q: Kubernetes was originally developed by which organization, and open-sourced in which year?
questions.e: Kubernetes was originally developed by Google and open-sourced in 2014. Docker Swarm, by contrast, came from Docker Inc. as its own built-in orchestration option.

questions.q: In Kubernetes architecture, what is the smallest deployable unit?
questions.e: A pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes and may contain one or more containers. A node is a worker machine running containerized applications, and a cluster is a set of nodes managed by Kubernetes — both are larger units than the pod.

questions.q: Within Kubernetes architecture, which element is responsible for managing the cluster's state and scheduling workloads?
questions.e: The control plane manages the cluster's state and workload scheduling. Nodes are the worker machines that actually run the containerized applications the control plane schedules onto them.

questions.q: Which Kubernetes capability is described as detecting and replacing failed containers?
questions.e: Self-healing is the capability that detects and replaces failed containers. Load balancing addresses a different concern — the efficient distribution of traffic — and automated scaling adjusts resources dynamically based on demand.

questions.q: Which security mechanism is listed among Kubernetes' benefits?
o: Role-based access control (RBAC) and secrets management
Mandatory two-factor authentication for all pods
questions.e: Kubernetes provides role-based access control and secrets management as its security features. Hardware-level isolation is characteristic of virtual machines rather than containers, which rely on operating system-level isolation.

questions.q: Comparing traditional, virtualized and container deployment stacks, which layers sit between the hardware and the applications in a virtualized deployment?
o: Operating system, then hypervisor, then a guest operating system and bin/library layer per virtual machine
Hypervisor only, with applications running directly on it
questions.e: In virtualized deployment the stack runs hardware, host operating system, hypervisor, then for each virtual machine a guest operating system, a bin/library layer, and the application. Container deployment replaces the hypervisor and per-VM guest operating systems with a single container runtime above one operating system, which is where the reduction in overhead comes from.

questions.q: In a container deployment stack, what sits directly above the operating system?
o: A guest operating system per container
questions.e: In container deployment the container runtime sits directly above the operating system, with each container adding only a bin/library layer and its application. There is no hypervisor and no per-container guest operating system, which distinguishes it from virtualized deployment.

questions.q: Which contrast between traditional and containerized deployment is drawn in relation to Kubernetes?
o: Traditional deployment involves manual installation, configuration and updates, while containerized deployment is automated and scalable
Traditional deployment is automated, while containerized deployment requires manual updates
Traditional deployment scales better than containerized deployment
questions.e: Traditional deployment requires manual installation, configuration and updates, whereas containerized deployment is automated and scalable, with Kubernetes adding centralized management of containerized applications. The Kubernetes advantage is framed as management centralisation rather than as the containerization itself.

questions.q: Compute services in the cloud are defined as the on-demand delivery of which resources?
o: Computing power, storage and networking resources
questions.e: Compute services refer to the on-demand delivery of computing power, storage and networking resources in the cloud, letting businesses deploy and manage applications without investing in physical hardware.

questions.q: Amazon EC2 stands for which of the following?
questions.e: EC2 stands for Elastic Compute Cloud, a web service providing resizable compute capacity in the AWS cloud. Amazon ECS, the Elastic Container Service, is a separate offering focused on container orchestration.

questions.q: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is best described as:
o: A firewall ruleset applied to an instance
A pre-configured package containing the operating system and applications required to launch an instance
A billing record for instance usage
A snapshot of an instance's memory at a point in time
questions.e: An AMI is a pre-configured package containing the operating system and the applications needed to launch an EC2 instance. Because a single AMI can launch many instances, it is the mechanism that provides consistency across development, testing and production environments.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the three types of Amazon Machine Images?
questions.e: AMIs come in three types: public AMIs shared across AWS users, private AMIs restricted to specific AWS accounts, and marketplace AMIs offered by third-party vendors. The categories describe sharing and sourcing rather than the operating system inside the image.

questions.q: Which EC2 feature acts as a firewall controlling traffic to instances?
questions.e: Security groups act as a firewall controlling inbound and outbound traffic to EC2 instances. Elastic IPs provide static public addressing, and Elastic Block Store provides persistent storage — neither filters traffic.

questions.q: Which EC2 feature provides persistent storage for instances?
questions.e: Elastic Block Store provides persistent storage for EC2 instances, meaning data survives beyond the life of the running instance. Auto Scaling and CloudWatch address instance count and monitoring respectively, not storage durability.

questions.q: Which AWS service is integrated with EC2 for monitoring and performance tracking, collecting data to help optimize resource use and troubleshoot issues?
questions.e: Amazon CloudWatch monitors and manages AWS resources and applications, collecting data that helps users optimize resource use, respond to performance changes and troubleshoot. CloudFront is a content delivery network, and CloudTrail is an auditing and compliance tool that records API activity.

questions.q: Which EC2 instance family is described as providing balanced compute, memory and networking, with t3 and m5 as examples?
questions.e: General Purpose instances such as t3 and m5 provide balanced compute, memory and networking, and are suited to web servers and applications. Compute Optimized instances such as c5 and c6g instead prioritise high-performance processing.

questions.q: Instances in the r5 and x1e families belong to which EC2 instance category?
questions.e: The r5 and x1e families are Memory Optimized instances, intended for large memory workloads such as in-memory databases and caching. Storage Optimized instances are the i3 and d2 families, aimed at high IOPS and large storage needs.

questions.q: GPU and FPGA instances such as p3 and g4 fall under which EC2 category, and what use cases are they matched with?
o: Storage Optimized, for high IOPS workloads
Accelerated Computing, for machine learning and gaming
questions.e: The p3 and g4 families are Accelerated Computing instances offering GPU and FPGA hardware, matched with machine learning and gaming workloads. Data analytics and real-time processing are instead paired with Compute Optimized instances.

questions.q: Which EC2 instance category is recommended for in-memory databases and caching?
questions.e: In-memory databases and caching map to Memory Optimized instances, the family built for large memory workloads. Storage Optimized instances address a different bottleneck: high IOPS and large amounts of attached storage.

questions.q: Which placement group type is designed to deliver low-latency, high-bandwidth networking between instances?
questions.e: Cluster placement groups provide low-latency, high-bandwidth networking and are matched with high-performance computing. Partition placement reduces the impact of hardware failures, and spread placement distributes instances across multiple hardware nodes.

questions.q: Which placement group type distributes instances across multiple hardware nodes and is recommended for critical applications needing isolation?
questions.e: Spread placement distributes instances across multiple distinct hardware nodes and suits critical applications requiring isolation. Partition placement is the neighbouring option, but it is aimed at reducing the impact of hardware failures for large-scale distributed systems rather than isolating individual critical instances.

questions.q: Which placement group type is matched with large-scale distributed systems and reducing the impact of hardware failures?
questions.e: Partition placement reduces the impact of hardware failures and is recommended for large-scale distributed systems. Cluster placement serves the opposite priority — packing instances closely for network performance rather than separating them for fault tolerance.

questions.q: Reserved Instances involve committing to usage for which durations in exchange for cost savings?
questions.e: Reserved Instances require a commitment of either 1 or 3 years in return for cost savings, making them suited to long-term steady-state workloads. On-Demand instances, by contrast, are billed by the hour or second with no such commitment.

questions.q: Which EC2 pricing model involves purchasing unused EC2 capacity at discounted rates?
questions.e: Spot Instances let you purchase unused EC2 capacity at discounted rates, which is why they are matched with fault-tolerant, flexible workloads that can survive interruption. Dedicated Hosts are a different model entirely: physical servers dedicated to a single customer.

questions.q: Which pricing model is recommended for short-term, unpredictable workloads?
questions.e: On-Demand Instances suit short-term, unpredictable workloads because capacity is paid for by the hour or second with no commitment. Reserved Instances are the recommendation for the opposite profile — long-term, steady-state workloads.

questions.q: Dedicated Hosts as an EC2 pricing model are defined as:
o: Instances billed per second with no commitment
Physical servers dedicated to one customer
A flexible pricing commitment across instance families
Discounted spare capacity sold at fluctuating prices
questions.e: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers dedicated to a single customer. Savings Plans are the separate flexible pricing model aimed at long-term cost efficiency, and Spot Instances are the discounted spare-capacity option.

questions.q: In EC2 security, at which level do Network ACLs operate?
questions.e: Network ACLs act as an additional layer of security at the subnet level, complementing security groups, which control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. Having both means traffic can be filtered twice on its way to an instance.

questions.q: Which EC2 security feature uses public-private key cryptography to provide secure access to instances?
questions.e: Key pairs use public-private key cryptography for secure access to instances. Security groups and network ACLs filter traffic rather than authenticating a user's session, and Elastic IPs simply provide stable addressing.

questions.q: Which mechanism provides secure role-based access control for EC2 instances?
questions.e: IAM roles provide secure role-based access control for instances. A VPC serves a different purpose — creating an isolated network in which the instances run — and key pairs handle cryptographic login rather than permission scoping.

questions.q: Encryption for EC2 data is described as being implemented using which combination?
questions.e: EC2 data encryption uses AWS KMS (Key Management System) together with SSL/TLS. IAM roles and security groups address access control and traffic filtering rather than encrypting the data itself.

questions.q: Which EC2 benefit is described as the ability to increase or decrease capacity within minutes?
questions.e: Elastic Web-Scale Computing is the benefit defined as increasing or decreasing capacity within minutes. Complete Control refers instead to having full administrative access to instances, and Flexible Hosting to the choice of operating system, software and configuration.

questions.q: Which EC2 feature automatically adjusts the number of running instances based on demand?
questions.e: Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number of instances in response to demand. Placement groups influence where instances are physically located to meet performance or fault-tolerance goals, but they do not change how many instances run.

questions.q: AWS is described as a cloud computing platform developed by combining which three categories of offering?
questions.e: AWS is characterised as a comprehensive, evolving platform offering services as building blocks, developed by combining infrastructure as a service, platform as a service and packaged software as a service offerings. The 'building blocks' framing is why a single AWS account can span raw compute through to finished applications.

questions.q: AWS is reported as generating how much in net sales in 2019?
questions.e: AWS generated 35.03 billion U.S. dollars in 2019 net sales. The 100 billion figure refers to the size of the global cloud market that AWS leads, and the 10 billion figure to the quarterly revenue record AWS broke in the first quarter of 2020.

questions.q: AWS is said to control what share of the cloud market, while generating roughly what revenue relative to its closest rival?
o: More than half the market, and three times the revenue of its closest rival
More than a third of the market, and twice the revenue of its closest rival
About a quarter of the market, and equal revenue to its closest rival
About 76% of the market, and ten times the revenue of its closest rival
questions.e: AWS is described as controlling more than a third of the cloud market while generating twice the revenue of its closest rival, in a global cloud market led at the 100 billion dollar level. It also broke the record of being a 10 billion dollar business in the first quarter of 2020.

questions.q: Which companies are named among the top 10 AWS users based on monthly EC2 spend?
questions.e: Netflix, Twitch, LinkedIn and Facebook are named among the top 10 AWS users, with the ranking based specifically on monthly EC2 spend rather than total AWS spend. AWS is credited with over one million global users overall.

questions.q: AWS availability is described as spanning how many countries, offering how many fully-featured services, across how many availability zones?
questions.e: AWS availability is stated as spanning 245 countries worldwide with over 175 fully-featured services from data centers across 76 availability zones. Note that the 245 figure is internally questionable, since it exceeds the number of countries that exist; the same 175-service count reappears in the discussion of pay-as-you-go pricing.

questions.q: Which AWS advantage is explained by the claim that the more you use a service, the less you pay per unit?
questions.e: Cost-effectiveness covers pay-as-you-go, scalable pricing in which you pay only for what you use and each unit costs less with each new purchase. Flexibility is a separate advantage concerning platform agnosticism toward operating systems and languages.

questions.q: The AWS advantage of 'flexibility' is defined in terms of which property?
o: Being platform agnostic to operating systems and languages, with no rigid protocols or restrictions
Charging less per unit as usage increases
The ability to scale capacity up and down on demand
Running on a safe and secure infrastructure
questions.e: Flexibility refers to AWS having no rigid protocols or restrictions and being platform agnostic toward operating systems and languages, so businesses can select whichever programming model or development platform suits them. Scaling on demand is instead covered by elasticity and scalability.

questions.q: For a beginner's introduction, AWS is broken down into which three main products?
questions.e: For introductory purposes AWS is broken into three main products: EC2 as Amazon's virtual machine service, Glacier as a low-cost cloud storage service, and S3 as Amazon's storage system. This is a deliberate simplification, since the same material goes on to describe over thirty individual AWS services.

questions.q: Amazon S3 stands for which of the following, and what is it used for?
o: Simple Streaming Service, used for real-time data feeds
Simple Storage Service, used for scalable object storage for internet backup, collection and analytics
Secure Storage Service, used for encrypted key management
Scalable Server Service, used for hosting virtual machines
questions.e: S3 is the Simple Storage Service, used for scalable object storage supporting internet backup, collection and analytics, and described as the cheapest option in the object-storage category. Real-time data streaming is handled by Amazon Kinesis, a different service.

questions.q: Besides S3, which services are listed in the AWS 'storage' domain?
o: Elastic Block Store, Amazon Glacier and AWS Snowball
questions.e: The storage domain also includes Elastic Block Store, Amazon Glacier and AWS Snowball. RDS, Aurora and Redshift are grouped instead under data migration, collection and transfer products.

questions.q: Amazon KMS is described as a security tool using encryption of what strength?
questions.e: Amazon KMS, the Key Management System, is described as using 256-bit encryption for data security to safeguard data from hackers and cyber-attacks. The 256 and 512 figures also appear in hashing contexts as SHA-256 and SHA-512, which are hash functions rather than encryption schemes.

questions.q: Amazon Lambda's cost model is based on what?
o: How long it takes the customer to execute the code
The number of API calls registered in DNS
The number of instances reserved per year
questions.e: Lambda provides serverless compute in which payment depends on how long the customer's code takes to execute, with the service running code in response to specific events and managing the dependent resources. There is no instance to reserve, which is what distinguishes it from EC2's pricing models.

questions.q: Amazon Route 53 is best described as which kind of service?
o: A cloud-based Domain Name System web service that does not require a separate DNS account
questions.e: Route 53 is a highly scalable, cloud-based Domain Name System web service that removes the need to maintain a separate DNS account, and it also provides domain name registration. CloudFront is the separate service that acts as a content delivery network.

questions.q: Which AWS service is described as an automated security assessment service that analyzes application behavior to identify potential security issues?
questions.e: Amazon Inspector is the automated security assessment service that analyzes application behaviour to identify potential security issues. CloudTrail is a related but distinct governance tool that provides visibility into user activity by recording API activity on the account.

questions.q: AWS CloudTrail is characterised as a tool for which purpose?
o: Converting media files in the cloud
Auditing, compliance monitoring and governance by recording API activity on the user account
Coordinating parallel or sequential processing steps
questions.e: CloudTrail is a web-based auditing, compliance monitoring and governance tool that increases visibility into user activity by recording API activity made on the account. Coordinating parallel or sequential processing steps is the role of Amazon Simple Workflow, and media conversion belongs to Elastic Transcoder.

questions.q: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce) is described as enabling which category of tasks?
o: Managing Docker containers across a cluster
Big data tasks such as web indexing, data mining and log file analysis
questions.e: EMR enables big data tasks including web indexing, data mining and log file analysis. Managing Docker containers across a cluster of EC2 instances is Amazon ECS, and certificate provisioning is handled by Certificate Manager.

questions.q: Which AWS service is defined as an easy-to-use application container for deploying and managing web applications?
questions.e: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is the easy-to-use application container for deploying and managing web applications. OpsWorks is described differently, as a DevOps platform managing applications of any scale or complexity.

questions.q: Amazon DynamoDB is characterised as which kind of data store?
o: A file storage service for EC2 instances
A scalable NoSQL data store managing distributed replicas of data for high availability
questions.e: DynamoDB is a scalable NoSQL data store that manages distributed replicas of data to make it highly available. The petabyte-scale data warehouse description belongs to Amazon Redshift, and the file storage service for EC2 instances is Amazon EFS.

questions.q: Amazon Redshift is described as which type of service?
o: A fast, fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse allowing analysis with existing business intelligence tools
An in-memory caching layer for real-time analytics
A managed search and analytics engine
questions.e: Redshift is a fast, fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse that supports easy data analysis using a customer's existing business intelligence tools. The managed open-source search and analytics engine is the Elasticsearch Service, a separate offering.

questions.q: ElastiCache improves application performance by allowing users to retrieve information from what?
questions.e: ElastiCache improves application performance by letting users retrieve information from an in-memory caching system, and is popular for real-time analytics, caching, gaming, session stores, geospatial services and queuing. Cold-storage archiving is instead the role of Glacier.

questions.q: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service) is described as which of the following?
o: A reliable and highly scalable hosted queue for storing messages as they travel between computers
A notification tool that push-sends messages to subscribers via email or SMS
An email sending and receiving service
A workflow coordinator for parallel or sequential processing steps
questions.e: SQS is a reliable and highly scalable hosted queue for storing messages while they travel between computers. Push-sending messages to large numbers of subscribers by email or SMS is Amazon SNS, and coordinating processing steps within an application is Amazon SWF.

questions.q: AWS Storage Gateway serves which purpose?
o: Securely integrating an organization's on-premises IT environments with AWS cloud storage for backup and disaster recovery
Distributing content to end users with low latency
Encrypting data at rest inside S3 buckets
Launching AWS resources in a private, isolated cloud
questions.e: Storage Gateway securely integrates an organization's on-premises IT environments with AWS cloud storage infrastructure for backup and disaster recovery. Launching resources in a private isolated cloud is the function of Amazon VPC.

questions.q: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) exists to manage, provision and deploy which artifacts?
o: Encryption keys for data at rest
Public SSL/TLS certificates for AWS-based websites and applications
questions.e: ACM lets customers easily manage, provision and deploy public Secure Sockets Layer / Transport Layer Security certificates for their AWS-based websites and applications. Managing encryption keys is the role of KMS, and DNS records belong to Route 53.

questions.q: AWS CloudFormation is defined as the service that does what?
o: Creates and updates a collection of related AWS resources in a simple and predictable way
Distributes content to end users through a global CDN
Migrates databases to the cloud with minimal downtime
Provides a cost-effective managed search solution
questions.e: CloudFormation lets users create and update a collection of related AWS resources in a simple, predictable way. Database migration with minimized downtime is instead the Database Migration Service, and the managed search solution is CloudSearch.

questions.q: AWS Data Pipeline is described as a lightweight orchestrated service for which kind of workflow?
o: Periodic, data-driven workflows moving data between AWS compute and storage services and on-premises data sources
Real-time streaming ingestion at millisecond latency
Serverless function execution triggered by events
questions.e: Data Pipeline is a lightweight orchestrated service for periodic, data-driven workflows, enabling reliable processing and movement of data between AWS compute and storage services and on-premises sources. Real-time streaming is the domain of Amazon Kinesis, and event-triggered serverless execution is Lambda.

questions.q: In the Unilever case study, the company was spread across how many countries, and how many digital marketing web properties did the AWS migration support?
questions.e: Unilever was spread across 170 countries, and after migrating it used the full range of AWS services to support its 1700 digital marketing web properties. Its original problem was that on-premise data centers with differing processes and technologies could not deliver fast enough time-to-market for pilot campaigns.

questions.q: Which programming languages are named as examples an AWS architect should be able to write code in?
o: Java, Python or C+, or any language with an official AWS SDK
questions.e: An AWS architect should be able to write code in Java, Python or C+, or any other programming language that has an official AWS SDK. The SDK availability, rather than the language itself, is the actual criterion.

questions.q: Which automation and continuous integration tools are named among the 'other skills' expected of an AWS professional?
o: Terraform for automation, and CircleCI for CI
Ansible for automation, and Travis for CI
Chef or Puppet for automation, and Jenkins for CI
Docker for automation, and Kubernetes for CI
questions.e: Experience with automation tools like Chef or Puppet and familiarity with CI tools like Jenkins are listed among the additional expected skills, alongside code deployment knowledge and build and release management across multiple environments.

questions.q: AWS certification has been available since which year, and the role-based certifications cover which four roles?
o: 2013; Cloud Practitioner, Architect, Developer and Operations
questions.e: AWS certification has been available since 2013, with role-based certifications in Cloud Practitioner, Architect, Developer and Operations roles.

questions.q: Which networking services are specifically named as the ones an AWS professional should know for designing cloud networking with public and private subnets and VPC peering?
o: Route 53 for DNS, VPC, and CloudFront for CDN
Direct Connect, Transit Gateway and Global Accelerator
questions.e: Route 53 for DNS, Virtual Private Cloud, and CloudFront for content delivery are named as the services used to design cloud networking with public and private subnets, VPC peering and internet access. Networking terms an architect should understand include HTTP, VPN, DNS, CDN and TCP/IP.

questions.q: Microservices are defined as an architectural approach in which software is composed of small independent services that communicate over what?
o: Direct function calls into a shared codebase
questions.e: Microservices are small independent services communicating over well-defined APIs, owned by small self-contained teams. Communication through APIs rather than shared code is what allows each service to be developed, deployed and scaled independently.

questions.q: The 'autonomous' characteristic of microservices includes which specific constraint?
o: A single shared runtime for all services
One deployment pipeline for the whole application
questions.e: Autonomy means each service can be developed, deployed, operated and scaled independently, with no code sharing between services and communication occurring via well-defined APIs. A mandatory common language would contradict the separate benefit of technological freedom.

questions.q: The 'specialized' characteristic of microservices holds that as services grow complex, they should be:
o: Rewritten in a single shared language
Broken down into even smaller services
Merged into a larger service for efficiency
questions.e: Each service is focused on a specific task and is lightweight and purpose-built; as services grow complex they can be broken down into even smaller services. Merging them would work against the specialisation that gives microservices their modularity.

questions.q: Which benefit of microservices is described in terms of small independent teams taking ownership within well-understood, smaller scopes?
questions.e: Agility is the benefit describing small independent teams taking ownership within smaller, well-understood scopes, producing shorter development cycles and higher organizational throughput. Flexible scaling is a separate benefit concerning infrastructure allocation per feature demand.

questions.q: 'Graceful degradation', in which some functionality continues even during partial failures, is presented as part of which microservices benefit?
questions.e: Resilience covers the property that failure of one service does not crash the whole system, with graceful degradation letting some functionality continue during partial failures. This improves fault isolation and overall system reliability.

questions.q: Which microservices benefit is described as removing any enforced 'one size fits all' approach to tools and technologies?
questions.e: Technological Freedom means there is no enforced one-size-fits-all choice of tools and technologies, so teams can select optimal technology stacks. Reusable code is a distinct benefit about modular, function-specific services being reused across features.

questions.q: The claim that a 'low cost of failure encourages innovation' is presented as part of which microservices benefit?
questions.e: Easy Deployment covers support for CI/CD pipelines, easier rollback and experimentation, and a low cost of failure that encourages innovation, resulting in faster delivery of new features. Resilience concerns runtime fault isolation rather than the cost of deploying changes.

questions.q: A monolithic architecture is defined as one in which the entire program is constructed as what?
o: A single, indivisible unit with data access layer, business logic and user interface tightly integrated
A layered system with independently deployable tiers
A set of loosely coupled services
questions.e: In a monolithic architecture the entire program is a single indivisible unit, with the data access layer, business logic and user interface deployed and integrated tightly together. The direct consequence is that any change or update requires modifying and redeploying the entire monolith.

questions.q: Which is listed as a benefit of monolithic architecture in relation to testing and debugging?
o: End-to-end testing operations are enacted from a central logging system
Each module can be tested in complete isolation
Distributed tracing across services is automatic
questions.e: Monolithic architectures make testing and debugging less involved because end-to-end testing operations are enacted from a central logging system. Distributed tracing across multiple services and teams is the corresponding difficulty on the microservices side.

questions.q: Monolithic architecture is credited with 'boosted security' on what grounds?
o: It encrypts all internal communication by default
It isolates each module in its own runtime
