It requires multi-factor authentication for deployment
It is a closed system whose data processing activities are fully contained
questions.e: The security claim rests on a monolith being a closed system whose data processing activities are fully contained and therefore protected against cyberthreats. This claim sits in some tension with the same material's summary table, which rates monolithic deployment risk as high because the architecture is a single point of failure.

questions.q: Which pair is identified as the drawbacks of monolithic architecture?
o: High licensing costs, and slow networking
Resistance to new technologies, and reduced scalability
questions.e: The two named drawbacks are resistance to new technologies, because monolithic applications are typically tightly coupled, and reduced scalability, since even minor scaling may require effectively dismantling and rebuilding the system. Complex debugging and coordination overhead are drawbacks of microservices instead.

questions.q: With regard to deployment, how do monolithic and microservices architectures differ?
o: Monolithic deploys each module separately, while microservices deploy as one package
Monolithic requires containerization, while microservices do not
Both deploy as a single package, but microservices require containers
Monolithic uses one-package deployment with a simple setup, while microservices deploy each service independently, often containerized, with a more complex setup
questions.e: Monolithic deployment is a single package with a simple setup, whereas microservices deploy each service independently, are often containerized for consistency, and involve a more complex setup. Containerization appears on the microservices side precisely because independent services need consistent runtime environments.

questions.q: Regarding modifications and updates, which statement describes the monolithic architecture?
o: Changes are automatically isolated to one module
Tight coupling causes ripple effects, changes require a full system redeploy, and retesting overhead is high
Continuous deployment workflows are natively supported
Individual components can be modified and deployed independently
questions.e: In a monolith, tight coupling causes ripple effects, changes require redeploying the whole system, and retesting overhead is high. Independent modification and support for continuous deployment workflows are the corresponding microservices properties.

questions.q: With respect to scalability, what is the specific inefficiency of the monolithic approach?
o: Scaling requires rewriting all services in a new language
The entire application must be scaled to meet one module's needs, leading to resource wastage
Only the high-demand module can be scaled, starving other modules
questions.e: A monolith must be scaled in its entirety to satisfy a single module's needs, which wastes resources. Microservices scale only the high-demand service, giving more efficient resource allocation and supporting distributed systems.

questions.q: In the operational impact comparison, how is deployment risk rated for each architecture?
o: Monolithic: low, because it is a closed system; Microservices: high, because of distribution
Monolithic: high, because it is a single point of failure; Microservices: low, because failure is isolated
questions.e: Deployment risk is rated high for monolithic architecture because it is a single point of failure, and low for microservices because failure is isolated. Total cost of ownership follows the same pattern: higher for monoliths, which must be upgraded as a whole, and lower for microservices, which are scaled and maintained selectively.

questions.q: In the summary comparison of the two architectures, how does testing compare?
o: Testing is easier for monolithic (end-to-end), and harder for microservices, which need integration testing
Both require identical integration testing effort
Testing is harder for monolithic and easier for microservices
questions.e: Testing is rated easier for monolithic architecture because it can be done end-to-end, and harder for microservices because integration testing across services is required. This is one of the few dimensions on which the monolith is rated the easier option, alongside initial development simplicity.

questions.q: How is the development experience of each architecture summarised over the lifetime of a project?
o: Monolithic is complex initially but becomes simple; microservices stay complex throughout
Monolithic is simpler initially but grows complex; microservices are more complex initially but easier to manage as they grow
Microservices are simpler at every stage of the project
Both are equally simple at every stage
questions.e: Monolithic development is simpler initially and becomes complex as the system grows, while microservices are more complex initially but easier to manage as they grow. This crossover is the reason the recommendation depends on expected project scale rather than being universal.

questions.q: In the comparison of team structures, which arrangement matches each architecture?
o: Monolithic: a single large team; Microservices: multiple small teams
Monolithic: multiple small teams; Microservices: a single large team
Both use a single large team
questions.e: A monolith is associated with a single large team, while microservices are associated with multiple small teams. This mirrors the definition of microservices as services owned by small, self-contained teams.

questions.q: Which scenario is marked as favouring monolithic architecture rather than microservices?
o: Limited resources and small team size
questions.e: Limited resources or small team size favours monolithic architecture, as do small applications. Large complex applications, rapid development and deployment, independent scaling and technology diversity all favour microservices.

questions.q: Why are startups presented as a good fit for monolithic architecture?
o: Because a monolith can be built cost-effectively by lean development teams without imposing too steep a learning curve
Because monoliths scale individual features more cheaply
Because startups need maximum technology diversity from day one
Because startups always have large DevOps teams available
questions.e: Startups need flexibility and start-up funding, and a monolith can be constructed cost-effectively by lean development teams without imposing a steep learning curve. Microservices, by contrast, typically require trained DevOps teams to implement and administer.

questions.q: Which company is cited as having transitioned from a monolithic architecture to a cloud-based microservices architecture, with a backend containing substantial load balancer support?
questions.e: Netflix is cited as the entertainment platform that moved from a monolithic architecture to a cloud-based microservices architecture, with its new backend containing plenty of load balancer support to optimize workloads. Amazon appears in the neighbouring ecommerce example rather than as the migration case.

questions.q: In the ecommerce use case for microservices, what figure is given for the size of the 2023 ecommerce sales market?
questions.e: The 2023 ecommerce sales market is stated as topping 5.8 trillion USD, cited alongside Amazon as an example of retailers driving sales through convenience and faster delivery on microservices architecture.

questions.q: The 'toughest jobs' use case for microservices is justified on what grounds?
o: Microservices remove the need for testing
Ongoing microservices use typically requires the implementation and administration skills of trained DevOps teams, which is especially useful for complex applications
Microservices eliminate the need for coordination between teams
questions.e: The toughest jobs case rests on microservices requiring trained DevOps teams who can create the specific services the architecture needs, with those skills being especially valuable for complex applications. The staffing requirement is a cost of the approach, which is why it does not suit small teams.

questions.q: In terms of fault isolation, how do the two architectures compare?
o: Both isolate failures to individual modules
Neither architecture provides any fault isolation
In a monolith failure is isolated to one module, while in microservices it cascades
In a monolith failure affects the entire application, while in microservices failure is isolated to a single service
questions.e: A monolithic failure affects the entire application, whereas a microservices failure is isolated to a single service. This is why deployment risk is rated high for monoliths and low for microservices.

questions.q: Encryption is defined as the process of converting which of the following?
o: A hash back into its original message
A private key into a public key
Ciphertext into a fixed-length hash value
Readable plaintext into unreadable ciphertext to prevent unauthorized access
questions.e: Encryption converts readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable format (ciphertext) to prevent unauthorized access. Converting data into a fixed-length value that cannot be reversed is hashing, a fundamentally different operation because it is one-way.

questions.q: AES and RSA are given as examples of which encryption types respectively?
o: AES is symmetric; RSA is asymmetric
AES is asymmetric; RSA is symmetric
questions.e: AES is the example of symmetric encryption, which uses the same key for encryption and decryption, while RSA is the example of asymmetric encryption, which uses a public/private key pair. The key-count difference is what makes asymmetric encryption suitable for digital signatures.

questions.q: Which pair of examples is given for protecting data in transit versus data at rest?
o: In transit: databases and backups; at rest: HTTPS and VPNs
In transit: HTTPS and VPNs; at rest: databases and backups
In transit: SAML; at rest: OAuth 2.0
In transit: hashing; at rest: digital signatures
questions.e: HTTPS and VPNs are the examples of protecting data in transit, while databases and backups are the examples of data at rest. The distinction matters operationally because best practice is to encrypt in both states rather than choosing one.

questions.q: Which property distinguishes hashing from encryption?
o: Hashing is a one-way function producing a fixed-length value that cannot be reversed
Hashing produces variable-length output that depends on input size
Hashing uses a public/private key pair
questions.e: Hashing is a one-way function converting data into a fixed-length hash value that cannot be reversed, which is why it verifies integrity rather than providing confidentiality. Encryption, by contrast, is designed to be reversed by whoever holds the correct key.

questions.q: Which hash functions are named as common choices in cloud security?
questions.e: SHA-256 and SHA-512 are the named common hash functions, used for password verification, file integrity and version control in cloud storage. AES and RSA are encryption algorithms rather than hash functions, despite also being identified by key or digest size.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of hashing in cloud security?
o: Ensuring data integrity, so that changes to data can be detected
Providing confidentiality for data in transit
Establishing a shared secret between two parties
questions.e: Hashing ensures data integrity by making changes to data detectable. It cannot provide confidentiality, since the operation cannot be reversed to recover the original data for a legitimate recipient.

questions.q: In creating a digital signature, what does the sender do?
o: Encrypts the whole message with a symmetric key and appends the key
Sends the plaintext hash without any encryption
Hashes the message and encrypts the hash using the recipient's public key
Hashes the message and encrypts the hash using their own private key
questions.e: The sender hashes the message and encrypts the resulting hash with their own private key; the recipient then decrypts the signature using the sender's public key and compares hashes. Using the sender's private key is what makes the signature attributable, and therefore what enables non-repudiation.

questions.q: Which three benefits are attributed to digital signatures?
questions.e: Digital signatures provide integrity, authentication and non-repudiation, because they combine hashing with asymmetric encryption. Confidentiality is not among them: a signature proves who sent a message and that it is unaltered, but does not by itself hide its contents.

questions.q: Within Public Key Infrastructure, which component is responsible for verifying identities?
questions.e: The Registration Authority verifies identities, while the Certificate Authority issues the certificates and the Certificate Revocation List records certificates that are no longer valid. The split exists so that identity vetting and certificate issuance are distinct responsibilities.

questions.q: Identity and Access Management systems are built on which two core functions?
o: Authentication, verifying identity, and authorization, granting permissions
questions.e: IAM rests on authentication, which verifies identity, and authorization, which grants permissions. Confusing the two is a common error: authentication establishes who a principal is, while authorization determines what that principal may do.

questions.q: In IAM terminology, roles are best described as:
o: Collections of users grouped for convenience
JSON documents specifying allowed and denied actions
questions.e: Roles are temporary identities carrying permissions. Policies are the JSON documents that specify allowed or denied actions, and users and groups represent the people or processes themselves.

questions.q: IAM policies take which format?
o: JSON documents specifying allowed or denied actions
questions.e: IAM policies are JSON documents that specify allowed or denied actions. They are attached to users, groups or roles, and are governed by the principle of least privilege, which says to give users only the access they need.

questions.q: The principle of least privilege states that:
o: Users should be given only the access they need
Every user should have identical permissions for consistency
Permissions should be granted broadly and revoked after audit
Administrators should hold all permissions centrally
questions.e: Least privilege means giving users only the access they actually need. Granting broadly and revoking later inverts the principle and leaves a window in which excess permissions can be exploited.

questions.q: Which protocols are named as the common protocols used for Single Sign-On?
questions.e: SAML, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect are the named SSO protocols. SSO allows a user to log in once and reach multiple services, improving user experience, reducing the number of passwords and lowering IT overhead.

questions.q: Federated identity management is best illustrated by which scenario?
o: A user logs in once and accesses multiple internal apps in the same company
An administrator assigns a JSON policy to a role
A firewall filters traffic at the subnet level
A student uses their university login to access Google Workspace
questions.e: Federated identity links identity systems across different organizations, illustrated by a student using their university login to access Google Workspace. Logging in once to reach multiple internal apps within one organization describes Single Sign-On instead.

questions.q: In the comparison of IAM, SSO and federated identity, what does each primarily control?
o: IAM controls identity across domains; SSO controls resources; federated identity controls sessions
IAM controls a single login session; SSO controls access to resources; federated identity controls internal apps
IAM controls access to resources; SSO controls a single login session; federated identity controls identity across domains
All three control access to resources equally
questions.e: IAM controls access to resources organization-wide, SSO controls a single login session across internal apps, and federated identity controls identity across domains and external organizations. The example given for each is AWS IAM, G Suite or Office 365, and a university login used to reach Elsevier.

questions.q: Which vendors are matched with their Security as a Service categories?
o: Okta for antivirus, Norton Cloud for DDoS protection, Cloudflare for email filtering, Proofpoint for identity
Proofpoint for DDoS protection, Cloudflare for antivirus, Okta for email filtering, Norton Cloud for identity
Cloudflare for identity management, Okta for DDoS protection, Norton Cloud for email filtering, Proofpoint for antivirus
Norton Cloud for antivirus, Cloudflare for DDoS protection, Okta for identity management, Proofpoint for email filtering
questions.e: SECaaS examples pair Norton Cloud with antivirus and antimalware, Cloudflare with DDoS protection, Okta with identity management, and Proofpoint with email filtering. The model's advantages are that it stays always updated, uses pay-as-you-go pricing, and scales.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among common cloud threats?
questions.e: Misconfigured cloud storage buckets are a listed common threat, alongside data breaches, insecure APIs, insider threats, account hijacking and DDoS attacks. Because misconfiguration is a settings problem rather than an attack, mitigation is framed as proactive configuration and monitoring.

questions.q: Under the shared responsibility model for public cloud, how are duties divided?
o: The provider secures everything including customer data
Responsibility rotates on a scheduled basis
The provider secures the cloud infrastructure, while the customer secures their data and configurations
The customer secures the physical data center, while the provider secures applications
questions.e: The provider secures the cloud infrastructure and the customer secures their own data and configurations, which is why customers must still enable logging, IAM, encryption and patching. AWS, Azure and GCP are the named examples of providers operating this way.

questions.q: Private cloud security is described as best suited to which sectors?
questions.e: Private cloud is presented as best for healthcare, finance and government, since it offers full control over hardware, data and policies and allows security controls to be tailored. It is often deployed on-premises or with a trusted third party.

questions.q: In the deployment model comparison, how are control and customization rated for a private cloud?
questions.e: Private cloud is rated as offering full control and high customization, whereas public cloud has limited control and minimal customization, and hybrid sits between them with mixed control and medium customization. Compliance follows the same pattern: easier to meet privately, varying publicly, and needing planning in a hybrid setup.

questions.q: How is security rated for the hybrid cloud in the deployment model comparison?
questions.e: Hybrid cloud security is rated 'complex', compared with 'shared' for public cloud and 'internal' for private cloud. The complexity comes from having to secure communication between the public and private environments using encryption, federated IAM and unified monitoring.

questions.q: Which compliance standard is specifically identified as covering payment card security?
questions.e: PCI DSS is the payment card security standard. ISO/IEC 27001 covers general information security, HIPAA covers U.S. healthcare protection, GDPR covers data protection for EU citizens, and NIST 800-53 covers U.S. government system controls.

questions.q: NIST 800-53 is identified as covering which domain?
o: General information security certification for any organization
questions.e: NIST 800-53 specifies U.S. government controls for systems. GDPR is the standard covering data protection for EU citizens, and ISO/IEC 27001 is the general information security standard.

questions.q: Which access control models are named among defense strategies for permissions in the cloud?
questions.e: Role-based access control or attribute-based access control are the named models for managing permissions, alongside encrypting data in transit and at rest, enabling multi-factor authentication, setting up security groups and network ACLs, and performing regular log audits with anomaly detection. SAML and OAuth are authentication protocols for SSO rather than permission models.

questions.q: In the hybrid cloud security example given, how does a bank divide its workloads?
o: Both web apps and transactions run on private servers with public backups
Transaction processing runs on public cloud while web apps stay private
All workloads run on public cloud with private encryption keys
Customer-facing web apps run on public cloud while transaction processing stays on private servers
questions.e: The bank example places customer-facing web applications on public cloud while keeping transaction processing on private servers. This split reflects the general logic of hybrid deployment: elastic, low-sensitivity workloads go public, and sensitive processing stays private.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the five key characteristics of cloud computing?
o: On-Demand Self-Service, Broad Network Access, Resource Pooling, Rapid Elasticity, Measured Service
questions.e: The five key characteristics are On-Demand Self-Service, Broad Network Access, Resource Pooling, Rapid Elasticity and Measured Service. IaaS, PaaS and SaaS are service models rather than characteristics, describing what is delivered rather than how cloud behaves.

questions.q: Machine learning is defined as a field of AI that gives systems the ability to do what?
o: Distribute computation across geographically dispersed machines
Store and retrieve large volumes of data efficiently
Automatically learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed
Follow explicitly programmed rules with greater speed
questions.e: Machine learning gives systems the ability to automatically learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed, using statistical techniques to improve performance on a task through exposure to data. Learning without explicit programming is precisely what separates ML from conventional rule-based software.

questions.q: Supervised learning is characterised by training on what kind of data?
o: Unlabeled data, to discover hidden patterns
Synthetic data generated by another model
Labeled data, where the desired output is known
questions.e: Supervised learning trains models on labeled data where the desired output is known. Training on unlabeled data to discover hidden patterns is unsupervised learning, and learning from reward signals in an environment is reinforcement learning.

questions.q: Within supervised learning, what is the difference between classification and regression?
o: Both predict continuous values, but classification requires labeled data
Classification predicts categories or classes; regression predicts continuous values
Both predict categories, but regression is faster
Classification predicts continuous values; regression predicts categories
questions.e: Classification predicts categories or classes, with spam detection as the example, while regression predicts continuous values, with stock prices as the example. Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees and Linear Regression are the named supervised algorithms.

questions.q: K-Means Clustering and Principal Component Analysis are given as examples of which learning type?
questions.e: K-Means Clustering and Principal Component Analysis are the named unsupervised learning examples, which train on unlabeled data to discover hidden patterns. Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees and Linear Regression are the supervised counterparts.

questions.q: Within unsupervised learning, which technique identifies relationships between data items, as in market basket analysis?
questions.e: Association identifies relationships between data items, illustrated by market basket analysis. Clustering is the other unsupervised technique and instead groups similar data points, illustrated by customer segmentation.

questions.q: Reinforcement learning trains agents to do what, and which algorithm is named as its example?
o: Reduce data dimensionality; Principal Component Analysis
Classify labeled inputs; Support Vector Machines
Group unlabeled points into clusters; K-Means
Make decisions in an environment to maximize rewards; Q-learning
questions.e: Reinforcement learning trains agents to make decisions within an environment so as to maximize rewards, with Q-learning as the named example and applications in robotics, game playing and autonomous systems. It requires neither labels nor a fixed dataset, which distinguishes it from both supervised and unsupervised approaches.

questions.q: What is the underlying reason cloud computing is presented as ideal for machine learning workloads?
o: ML models can only be written in cloud-hosted languages
ML requires large datasets and significant computational resources, and cloud offers those resources on demand
Cloud removes the need to evaluate models
questions.e: Machine learning requires large datasets and significant computational resources for training, and cloud computing supplies exactly that on demand. This is why cloud infrastructure is framed as providing scalability for ML, alongside accessibility, cost-efficiency, faster deployment and data management.

questions.q: In the cloud ML lifecycle, which stage uses services such as AWS Glue or Dataprep?
questions.e: Data preprocessing — cleaning and preparing data — uses services such as AWS Glue or Dataprep. Data ingestion is the preceding stage, which uploads data to cloud storage such as S3, GCS or Blob storage.

questions.q: Which services are named for the model training stage of the cloud ML lifecycle?
questions.e: Model training uses managed services such as SageMaker and Vertex AI with distributed computing. CloudWatch and Stackdriver appear at the opposite end of the lifecycle, in the monitoring stage used to track performance.

questions.q: In the cloud ML lifecycle, how are trained models served during deployment?
o: Through the training service's own console
Via REST APIs or edge devices
questions.e: Deployment serves models via REST APIs or on edge devices. Monitoring is treated as a separate subsequent stage, using tools such as CloudWatch or Stackdriver to track ongoing performance.

questions.q: Which AI services are correctly attributed to AWS?
o: Azure ML Studio and Cognitive Services
Vertex AI, BigQuery ML and Vision API
questions.e: SageMaker, Comprehend and Rekognition are the AWS AI services. Vertex AI, BigQuery ML and Vision API belong to Google Cloud, Azure ML Studio and Cognitive Services to Azure, and OCI AI Services to Oracle Cloud.

questions.q: Vertex AI, BigQuery ML and Vision API are the AI offerings of which cloud provider?
questions.e: Vertex AI, BigQuery ML and Vision API are Google Cloud's AI tools. Azure's corresponding offerings are Azure ML Studio and Azure Cognitive Services.

questions.q: Which challenge of cloud-based ML is defined as models becoming less accurate over time?
questions.e: Model drift is the challenge of ML models becoming less accurate over time, which is why best practice includes monitoring model performance and retraining regularly. Latency is a separate challenge affecting real-time applications due to data transfer.

questions.q: Which challenge of cloud-based ML arises directly from the pay-as-you-go billing model?
o: Cost management, since pay-as-you-go can lead to high expenses
questions.e: Cost management is the challenge attributed to the pay-as-you-go model, which can lead to high expenses if usage is not controlled. Notably, the same pay-as-you-go model is cited elsewhere as a cost-efficiency advantage because it removes upfront investment — the benefit and the risk come from the same mechanism.

questions.q: Which best practice is recommended for handling light ML workloads in the cloud?
o: Leverage serverless solutions such as AWS Lambda or Azure Functions
Train all models from scratch to maximise accuracy
questions.e: Serverless solutions such as AWS Lambda or Azure Functions are recommended for light workloads. Another cost-saving practice named alongside it is using pre-trained models where possible rather than training from scratch.

questions.q: Which emerging trend is defined as training models across decentralized devices without sharing raw data?
questions.e: Federated Learning trains models across decentralized devices without sharing raw data. Edge AI is a related but distinct trend concerned with bringing ML inference closer to the user via IoT and edge devices, rather than with how training data is kept private.

questions.q: AutoML is defined as automating which activity?
o: The process of selecting, training and tuning models
The deployment of containers across clusters
The routing of inference requests to edge devices
The encryption of training data at rest
questions.e: AutoML automates the selection, training and tuning of models. Explainable AI addresses a different goal — making models interpretable for compliance and transparency — rather than automating their construction.

questions.q: Which application of AI plus cloud is described as content creation using large language models, with ChatGPT and Bard as examples?
questions.e: Generative AI is content creation using large language models, exemplified by ChatGPT and Bard. Chatbots are listed separately as using natural language processing to answer customer queries, which is a narrower conversational application.

questions.q: How does AI change threat and security handling in the cloud, according to the comparison of clouds with and without ML?
o: It shifts from proactive anomaly detection to reactive detection
It replaces encryption with behavioural profiling
It removes the need for any security monitoring
It shifts from reactive detection to proactive anomaly detection, and from signature-based to pattern and behavior analysis
questions.e: With ML, security moves from reactive detection to proactive anomaly detection, and security detection moves from signature-based to pattern and behavior analysis. AI monitors network activity in real time and detects anomalies, phishing attempts and malware patterns, reducing response time.

questions.q: In the comparison of cloud capabilities with and without ML, how does resource scaling change?
o: From manual or rules-based, to predictive and autonomous
From predictive and autonomous, to manual or rules-based
It becomes scheduled rather than continuous
It remains manual in both cases
questions.e: Resource scaling moves from manual or rules-based without ML to predictive and autonomous with ML. Maintenance follows a parallel shift, from scheduled and manual to self-tuning systems.

questions.q: In the healthcare industry example, what are cloud-hosted ML models used for?
o: Dynamic pricing and personalized product recommendations
Predicting patient deterioration, classifying medical images and assisting in diagnostics
Crop health monitoring using satellite images
questions.e: In healthcare, cloud-hosted ML models predict patient deterioration, classify medical images and assist in diagnostics. Dynamic pricing and product recommendations belong to the e-commerce example, predictive maintenance to manufacturing, and crop health monitoring to agriculture.

questions.q: Which industry example is associated with fraud detection, credit scoring and customer churn prediction?
questions.e: Finance is associated with fraud detection, credit scoring and customer churn prediction. Transportation covers autonomous vehicles, traffic management and route optimization, while smart cities cover traffic prediction, surveillance and pollution monitoring using IoT and ML in the cloud.

questions.q: Which benefit of combining cloud and ML is described using the term 'Democratization of AI'?
o: The reduction of infrastructure costs through shared hardware
Making advanced AI capabilities broadly accessible, supported by pre-built cloud ML services and tools
The distribution of models across multiple geographic regions
The automatic explanation of model decisions to regulators
questions.e: Democratization of AI refers to advanced AI capabilities becoming broadly accessible, which cloud platforms enable by offering pre-built ML services and tools. Making models interpretable for compliance is a separate concept, covered under Explainable AI.
